result: Adenine base editors (ABEs) effectively downregulate PTBP1 in cell lines through splice site disruption. ABEs enable gene editing without DNA double-strand breaks and achieve high editing rates (up to 92.9% in Hepa cells) at splice donor sites, resulting in substantial reduction of PTBP1 transcript and protein levels across multiple cell lines (Hepa, N2a, C8-D1A).
evaluation: Claims C18-C28 and C81-C82 are well-supported by sequencing data (Figure 1 and supplements), RT-qPCR, and Western blot analyses showing consistent PTBP1 downregulation across cell lines. The methodology is validated with appropriate controls and multiple independent experiments.

result: 6-OHDA successfully induced a severe unilateral lesion in the nigrostriatal pathway of mice, characterized by 99% reduction in TH+ dopaminergic neurons in the SNc, 92% decrease in striatal DA fibers, increased astrocyte activation, and significant motor deficits including ipsilateral rotations and contralateral forelimb akinesia.
evaluation: Claims C29-C32 are supported by comprehensive histological quantification (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and behavioral testing with appropriate statistical analysis. The PD model is well-characterized and consistent with cited literature.

result: PTBP1 downregulation in neurons, but not astrocytes, of the SNc generates TH-expressing cells in a PD mouse model. AAV-hsyn treatment resulted in restoration of approximately 10% of TH+ cells in the lesioned SNc with confirmed base editing (~15%) and PTBP1 reduction (~25%), while AAV-GFAP treatment showed no effect above control levels.
evaluation: Claims C33-C34, C4, C37-C38, C59, C63-C64 are supported by histological quantification (Figure 2), molecular validation (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), and consistent with recent literature challenging astrocyte-to-neuron conversion. The cell-type specific effects are clearly demonstrated with appropriate promoters and controls.

result: TH+ cells generated in the SNc upon neuronal PTBP1 downregulation did not form striatal projections or restore the nigrostriatal pathway. No increase in DA fiber fluorescence was detected in the striatum or medial forebrain bundle despite the presence of TH+ cells in the SNc.
evaluation: Claims C35-C36, C60-C61 are supported by histological analysis (Figure 2E-F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4) showing no significant differences in striatal DA projections between treatment groups. This finding is consistent with cited work on PTBP1's role in axon regeneration.

result: PTBP1 downregulation in striatal neurons generates TH-expressing cells and rescues motor behaviors. AAV-hsyn treatment in the striatum resulted in ~106 TH+ cells per 3 sections with 23% base editing and 31% PTBP1 transcript reduction, leading to TH expression in non-dividing neurons.
evaluation: Claims C39-C41, C62, C5, C21 are supported by histological quantification (Figure 3A), molecular validation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), and BrdU labeling experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 6). The data consistently demonstrate TH induction in striatal neurons.

result: TH+ cells in the striatum originate from mature, non-dividing neurons. The majority of TH+ cells co-express NEUN (77.5-92%) and show no BrdU labeling (0/163 cells analyzed), indicating they arise from post-mitotic neurons rather than proliferating progenitors. These cells are morphologically distinct from endogenous DANs.
evaluation: Claims C42-C47, C64-C65 are supported by immunohistochemistry (Figure 3B-C), BrdU labeling (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), and morphometric analysis (Figure 3D). The absence of BrdU labeling in all 163 TH/NEUN+ cells provides strong evidence against de novo neurogenesis.

result: TH+ cells in the striatum are mature GABAergic neurons expressing dopaminergic markers. Multiplexed 4i imaging revealed that 75.2% of TH+ cells express DAT, 86.2% express NEUN, with minimal progenitor markers (<10%). Of TH/DAT/NEUN+ cells, 49.8% are GABAergic MSNs (CTIP2+) and 46.4% are GABAergic interneurons (PV/SST/CALB2+).
evaluation: Claims C48-C53, C8-C9 are supported by comprehensive 4i imaging data (Figure 4) with validated antibodies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The phenotypic characterization is thorough and demonstrates that TH expression occurs in multiple GABAergic neuronal subtypes.

result: PTBP1 downregulation in striatal neurons increases dopamine levels. AAV-hsyn-treated mice showed a 2.5-fold increase in striatal dopamine (4.4±2.6 vs 1.7±0.7 nmol/g protein, p=0.0159) and increased DOPAC (8.2±3.9 vs 3.1±1.8 nmol/g protein, p=0.0449) in the lesioned hemisphere.
evaluation: Claims C79-C80, C6, C73 are supported by HPLC quantification (Figure 3—figure supplement 4) with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. The dopamine increase is modest but statistically significant and correlates with TH expression.

result: Neuronal PTBP1 downregulation alleviates spontaneous motor dysfunctions in PD mice. AAV-hsyn treatment significantly improved forelimb akinesia (p<0.0001) and spontaneous rotations (p<0.0001) in both SNc and striatum, while AAV-GFAP treatment showed no significant effect.
evaluation: Claims C54-C56, C7, C20 are supported by behavioral testing data (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1) with appropriate statistical analysis and controls. The cell-type specific behavioral rescue is consistent with the histological findings.

result: PTBP1 downregulation does not rescue drug-induced motor behaviors. No recovery was observed in amphetamine-induced contralateral rotations or apomorphine-induced ipsilateral rotations in any treatment group, suggesting insufficient dopamine levels to reverse receptor hypersensitivity.
evaluation: Claims C57-C58, C77-C78 are supported by behavioral testing data (Figure 5C-D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The lack of drug-induced behavioral rescue is consistent with the modest dopamine increase and absence of nigrostriatal pathway reconstruction.

result: Off-target editing is minimal and does not contribute to TH expression. GUIDE-seq identified two off-target sites (Mypn and Ank1) with substantially lower editing rates (5.4-5.8%) than the on-target Ptbp1 site (23.0%), and no reduction in off-target gene transcript levels.
evaluation: Claims C83-C87 are supported by GUIDE-seq analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 3) and RT-qPCR validation. The comprehensive off-target analysis strengthens the conclusion that TH expression results from PTBP1 downregulation rather than off-target effects.

result: The local microenvironment contributes to TH expression induction. AAV-hsyn injection into the visual cortex did not induce TH expression in local neurons (0/174 Cas9/NEUN+ cells), suggesting region-specific factors are required.
evaluation: Claim C45 is supported by negative control experiment (Figure 3—figure supplement 5) and consistent with cited literature. However, the mechanism of microenvironmental influence remains unclear and requires further investigation.

result: PTBP1 is functionally expressed in mature neurons. Despite classical models suggesting negligible PTBP1 in mature neurons, loss-of-function mutations result in detectable protein reduction and behavioral improvements in PD mice, supported by recent findings of PTBP1 in axons of sensory and motor neurons.
evaluation: Claims C68-C69 are supported by Western blot data (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) showing PTBP1 expression in mature neurons and behavioral improvements upon downregulation. This challenges classical models and is corroborated by cited literature.

result: Local dopamine synthesis in striatal neurons may compensate for loss of SNc inputs. The authors propose that TH expression enabled local dopamine synthesis sufficient to restore function of MSNs and interneurons, with even modest dopamine increases rescuing spontaneous motor behaviors.
evaluation: Claims C71, C74-C75 are speculative inferences from the observed TH expression, dopamine increase, and behavioral improvements. While the hypothesis is plausible and supported by cited work (Delignat-Lavaud et al., 2023), direct evidence of local dopamine synthesis and release from TH+ neurons is lacking. Microdialysis or fiber photometry would be needed to confirm.

result: The manuscript contextualizes findings within established knowledge of PTBP1/nPTBP regulatory loops in neuronal differentiation, striatal circuitry, and dopamine-dependent motor control, citing appropriate literature to support the mechanistic framework.
evaluation: Claims C66-C67, C70, C72, C76 accurately represent cited literature and established knowledge. These provide appropriate context for interpreting the experimental findings.

result: The manuscript accurately describes established knowledge about Parkinson's disease pathology, current treatment limitations, and the role of tyrosine hydroxylase in dopamine synthesis.
evaluation: Claims C1, C10-C11, C22-C23 accurately represent well-established knowledge about PD and are appropriately cited. These provide necessary background context.

result: The manuscript accurately summarizes prior controversial work on PTBP1-mediated astrocyte-to-neuron conversion and subsequent studies questioning this model, providing appropriate context for the current investigation.
evaluation: Claims C2-C3, C15-C17 accurately represent cited prior work (Qian et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2022; Hoang et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2021) and frame the scientific controversy appropriately.

result: The manuscript accurately describes properties of astrocytes relevant to cell fate switching approaches, including their resistance to neurodegeneration, multipotency when activated, and proliferative capacity in brain injuries.
evaluation: Claims C12-C14 accurately represent cited literature about astrocyte properties and provide rationale for targeting these cells in regenerative approaches.
